angle: FastAPI Debugging: I Accidentally Created a Recursive Loop of Errors
hook: My FastAPI app started looping. Turns out, I was the problem.
audience: FastAPI developers, especially those new to recursion
caption: FastAPI loop? It was me. 🤦‍♂️ A recursive error. Learn to avoid this trap!

reel_script.visual: Close-up of a rapidly scrolling, chaotic FastAPI console log.
reel_script.voiceover: My FastAPI app just… exploded. Seriously.

reel_script.visual: Screen recording of the creator frantically typing in a debugger.
reel_script.voiceover: I was chasing an error. It pointed… somewhere else.

reel_script.visual: Animated loop visually representing a recursive function call.
reel_script.voiceover: Turns out, I’d built a loop of errors.

reel_script.visual: Creator smiling, pointing to a link in their caption.
reel_script.voiceover: Learn how to debug FastAPI like a pro! Link in bio.

problems: The reel script’s visuals are overly dramatic and potentially confusing for a general audience. The ‘chaotic console log’ and frantic debugging scene could be simplified. The length is too long for X and needs significant trimming. The hashtag usage is a bit heavy-handed.
fixes: Shorten Scene 1 to focus on the core issue – a recursive error. Replace the chaotic console log with a single, clearly highlighted line of code showing the recursive call. Trim Scene 2 to show only the essential debugging action. Reduce the caption to 240 characters or less, focusing on the core problem and solution. Limit hashtags to a maximum of two – consider #FastAPI or #Debugging. Consider a more concise voiceover for Scene 3, simply stating ‘recursive loop’ instead of ‘I’d built a loop of errors.’

caption_original: My FastAPI app started looping. Turns out, I was the problem. 🤦‍♂️ A recursive loop of errors – I’d accidentally created a feedback cycle of my own! Debugging FastAPI can be humbling. Especially when you're new to recursion. 😅
